title: Only 3% Of Adults Can Pass This Pilot Entrance Exam
summary: Explore pilot knowledge through clues, practical situations and fresh challenges.

landing.intro:
Read the skies and the clues.
Keep your thinking on course.

about.body: Connect the facts, notice the details and test your understanding of pilot knowledge. Each checkpoint reveals your topic profile before a different challenge begins.

steps: Read the clues and choose one answer.
See your topic profile at each checkpoint and continue to a new challenge.
Reveal your overall result, then optionally review the answers you missed.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an official pilot aptitude, licensing, medical, training or employment assessment. Always use approved aviation training and procedures.

next.tagline: Up next: Heading and ground track.
Up next: Decisions in changing conditions.

pilot-s1q1.question: Which force opposes an aircraft’s motion through the air?

pilot-s1q2.question: What does engine thrust primarily provide?

pilot-s1q3.question: In steady straight-and-level flight at constant speed, how do lift and weight compare?

answers.a1: They act in the same direction
answers.a4: Lift is always twice the weight

pilot-s1q4.question: What does the word airfoil describe?

answers.a1: Only the fuel inside a wing
answers.a4: A shape designed to produce an aerodynamic force as air flows around it

pilot-s1q5.question: Which part of an aircraft is its fuselage?

pilot-s1q6.question: What is the leading edge of a wing?

answers.a3: The aircraft and everything it carries

pilot-s2q1.question: On a conventional airplane, which control surface primarily controls pitch?

pilot-s2q2.question: Which control surfaces primarily control roll on a conventional airplane?

pilot-s2q3.question: Which control surface primarily controls yaw?

answers.a1: A change in cabin pressure only
answers.a2: The aircraft rotating around its nose-to-tail axis
answers.a3: The nose rotating up or down
answers.a4: The nose rotating left or right

answers.a2: An increase in fuel flow only
answers.a3: Rotation around the vertical axis only

answers.a1: The wings banking around the nose-to-tail axis
answers.a3: The nose rotating left or right around the vertical axis
answers.a4: A wheel turning on the ground only

pilot-s2q7.question: What do wing flaps change when extended?

pilot-s3q1.question: Which instrument shows pitch and bank relative to the horizon?

pilot-s3q2.question: What does a pressure altimeter use to estimate altitude?

pilot-s3q3.question: Why does the pressure setting on an altimeter matter?

answers.a3: It changes the aircraft’s actual mass

pilot-s3q4.question: What does an airspeed indicator primarily indicate?

answers.a1: Speed relative to the surrounding air, subject to instrument and pressure effects
answers.a4: Only speed relative to the ground

pilot-s3q5.question: What does a vertical speed indicator indicate?

pilot-s3q6.question: Which instrument uses Earth’s magnetic field to indicate direction?

pilot-s3q7.question: What does a fuel quantity indication tell a pilot?

answers.a2: The indicated amount of fuel remaining
answers.a4: The exact time of every future landing

pilot-s4q1.question: What does a weather forecast provide?

answers.a2: A guarantee of exact future conditions
answers.a4: An informed prediction that must be checked as conditions change

answers.a1: How far suitable objects can be seen and identified
answers.a3: Only the rate of fuel use

pilot-s4q3.question: Why can ice on a wing be hazardous?

answers.a2: It always increases lift without drag
answers.a3: It can change airflow and reduce performance

pilot-s4q4.question: Which statement about thunderstorms is sound?

answers.a1: They are harmless without visible lightning
answers.a2: They guarantee smooth air beneath them
answers.a3: They can contain several serious aviation hazards
answers.a4: They affect aircraft only on the ground

answers.a2: Wind with a component across the direction of travel
answers.a4: Wind that always matches the aircraft’s heading

answers.a2: A change in the aircraft registration
answers.a4: Irregular air movement that can disturb an aircraft’s motion

answers.a2: A change in wind speed or direction over a short distance
answers.a3: The temperature at which metal melts
answers.a4: A change in the aircraft’s paint

pilot-s5q1.question: A heading of 090° points approximately in which direction?

pilot-s5q2.question: A heading of 180° points approximately in which direction?

pilot-s5q3.question: A heading of 270° points approximately in which direction?

pilot-s5q4.question: A quarter-turn clockwise from north points where?

pilot-s5q5.question: A half-turn from east points where?

pilot-s5q6.question: An aircraft points south. Which direction is on its right?

pilot-s5q7.question: A map is drawn with north at the top. Which direction runs toward its lower left corner?

pilot-s6q2.question: With true airspeed unchanged, what does a direct headwind do to groundspeed?

pilot-s6q3.question: With true airspeed unchanged, what does a direct tailwind do to groundspeed?

pilot-s6q4.question: What is an aircraft’s ground track?

answers.a1: The line of its wing chord
answers.a2: The direction its nose must always point

pilot-s6q5.question: Why can heading and ground track differ?

answers.a2: Aircraft cannot travel sideways relative to their heading
Position east or west of the prime meridian
answers.a3: Position north or south of the equator

answers.a1: Position east or west of the prime meridian
answers.a2: Position north or south of the equator
answers.a3: The pressure in a fuel tank

pilot-s7q1.question: A route is 180 km and groundspeed is 120 km/h. How long does it take at that constant speed?

pilot-s7q2.question: A flight leg takes 40 minutes and the next takes 55 minutes. What is the combined time?

pilot-s7q3.question: For a calculation only, fuel use is 24 L per hour. How much is used in 30 minutes?

pilot-s7q4.question: A tank contains 90 L. A calculation predicts 35 L used on a leg. How much remains?

pilot-s7q5.question: An aircraft covers 60 km in 20 minutes. What is its average groundspeed?

pilot-s7q6.question: A schedule uses UTC throughout. Departure is 10:45 and flight time is 2 hours 20 minutes. What is arrival time?

pilot-s7q7.question: A loading example has 300 kg plus 2 loads of 45 kg each. What is the combined mass?

pilot-s8q1.question: An important instruction is unclear. What is the best response?

pilot-s8q2.question: What is the purpose of reading back a critical instruction?

answers.a1: To transfer all responsibility to the sender
answers.a2: To replace carrying out the confirmed instruction
answers.a3: To make the message longer for its own sake
answers.a4: To let the sender check that it was understood correctly

pilot-s8q3.question: Two tasks require the same person at the same time. What should be clarified?

answers.a1: Which task has the shorter name
answers.a4: Only the colour of the checklist

answers.a3: Only a reassurance that everything is fine
answers.a4: Relevant facts, unresolved concerns and the next required actions

pilot-s8q5.question: A colleague reports a new safety concern. What supports effective teamwork?

answers.a1: Dismiss it because the colleague is junior
answers.a2: Listen, clarify and address the concern
answers.a4: Hide it to protect the schedule

pilot-s8q6.question: A procedure changes. Which document should guide the task?

answers.a1: Any older copy that looks familiar
answers.a2: A remembered version from another organisation

pilot-s8q7.question: Why assign a clear owner to a follow-up action?

answers.a1: So the action becomes automatically complete
answers.a2: So nobody else may raise concerns
answers.a3: So responsibility and completion can be tracked

pilot-s9q1.question: Two people give different times for the same event. What is the best next step?

answers.a1: Average the times and call that a fact
answers.a2: Check each account against other reliable information
answers.a4: Choose the more confident speaker automatically

pilot-s9q2.question: Which statement records an observation rather than an assumption about motive?

answers.a1: The person left because they were guilty
answers.a2: The person intended to mislead everyone
answers.a3: The person never cared about the meeting
answers.a4: The person left the room at 14:10

pilot-s9q3.question: A photograph has no known date or location. What should be checked before relying on it?

answers.a3: Whether it matches a preferred conclusion

pilot-s9q4.question: A claim is repeated by three websites, all quoting one unnamed source. What does that show?

answers.a2: Repeated reporting, not three independent confirmations
answers.a3: Proof that the claim is accurate
answers.a4: Proof that no further checking is needed

pilot-s9q5.question: All authorised visitors have a pass. Mira has a pass. What follows from that rule alone?

answers.a1: It does not prove Mira is an authorised visitor
answers.a2: Mira cannot be an authorised visitor
answers.a3: Mira must be an authorised visitor

pilot-s9q6.question: A new reliable fact contradicts your initial explanation. What is the sound response?

answers.a2: Treat your first idea as unchangeable
answers.a3: Change the fact to fit the explanation

pilot-s9q7.question: A report says an event happened after a change. Does that timing alone prove the change caused it?

answers.a2: Yes; if the report is long enough
answers.a4: No; earlier events can never cause later ones

pilot-s10q1.question: Why use a checklist rather than memory alone?

answers.a2: To support consistent completion of required steps

answers.a1: Understanding relevant conditions and how they may develop
answers.a2: Watching one instrument and ignoring everything else

pilot-s10q3.question: A plan relied on conditions that have now changed. What is needed?

answers.a1: Continue only because time has already been spent
answers.a2: Reassess the plan using current information
answers.a4: Ignore the change if arrival is important

pilot-s10q4.question: Why is fatigue relevant to aviation decisions?

answers.a3: It removes the need for rest
answers.a4: It can impair attention and judgement

pilot-s10q5.question: A strong desire to arrive is influencing a safety decision. What should take priority?

answers.a1: The amount already paid for the trip
answers.a2: The actual conditions and applicable operating limits
answers.a3: The original promise regardless of conditions

pilot-s10q6.question: A warning conflicts with an apparently normal indication. What is the sound approach?

answers.a1: Cover the warning to reduce distraction
answers.a2: Choose whichever indication is more reassuring
answers.a3: Assume warnings can never be correct
answers.a4: Use the applicable procedure to assess the discrepancy

pilot-s10q7.question: Why keep alternatives in a flight plan?

answers.a1: A planned destination is always unavailable
answers.a3: Conditions may require a change of plan
